title: Cheeky Knight
summary: Let the pawn promote while rerouting the knight into a supported perpetual check.

nodes.question: Can White save the game without catching d4 directly?
nodes.explanation: The white king must support checks near the black king. The drawing plan changes the knight’s checking circuit rather than stopping the d-pawn.

nodes.question: How can Ne5 help while moving away from the king?
nodes.explanation: From e5 the knight attacks d3 and can reach c4. That route will let it capture b6 with check after promotion.

branches.title: Reroute into a perpetual-check circuit
commentary: Begin from the complete six-piece source board. The objective is to draw, not to win material.
Kc7 supports the corner checking circuit and restricts the opposing king’s escape squares.
d3 advances toward promotion, too far for a direct king chase.
Nc6+ checks Ka7 and forces the source’s corner retreat.
Ka8 leaves the knight without an immediate repeat of the same check, so White must reroute.
Ne5 attacks d3 and heads toward c4, preparing a different checking circuit.
d2 advances the attacked pawn instead of giving White time to capture it.
Nc4 attacks d2 and prepares Nxb6+, using Black’s own b-pawn as the entry to the corner.
d1=Q promotes. The new queen is far from the king and cannot break the forthcoming checks.
Nxb6+ captures the b6 pawn with check, reaching a square supported by Kc7.
Ka7 is the sole legal reply to this check: a6 is occupied and Kc7 controls b7 and b8.
Nc8+ checks Ka7 from the other supported square.
Ka8 is forced. Kc7 covers b8 and b7, while the a6 pawn blocks a6.
Nb6+ starts the same checking pattern again; this time b6 is empty.
Ka7 is again the only legal response.
Nc8+ returns to the second checking square without allowing the queen a useful turn.
Ka8 restores the same position for a second occurrence.
Nb6+ continues the independently extended repetition demonstration.
Ka7 is forced again; the king still has no second legal reply.
Nc8+ gives the final check in the encoded repetition cycle.
Ka8 produces a third occurrence of the same position with White to move. This is a claimable threefold repetition in the replay, in addition to the checked drawn tablebase result.
branches.classification: selected source perpetual with independent alternative extension to threefold repetition
branches.explanation: Ka8 produces a third occurrence of the same position with White to move. This is an actual threefold repetition in the replay, in addition to the checked drawn tablebase result.

branches.title: Chase the pawn with the king
commentary: Compare the source’s direct king approach instead of supporting the checking circuit.
Kd5 gives up the draw. The king is not close enough to the promotion square and has abandoned the necessary corner support.
d3 keeps Black’s exact win. The branch stops here rather than inventing a long queen conversion.
branches.explanation: d3 keeps Black’s exact win. The branch stops here rather than inventing a long queen conversion.

branches.title: Choose a knight square without the circuit
commentary: Compare an independent knight retreat after the first corner check.
Nd4 misses the c4–b6 checking route and changes the exact result to a Black win.
d2 keeps the passer moving. Black retains a checked forced win; promotion conversion is outside this comparison.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: d2 keeps the passer moving. Black retains a checked forced win; promotion conversion is outside this comparison.

exercises.prompt: Why does Ne5 save more than another immediate check?
exercises.answer: It attacks d3, then reaches c4, where the knight can capture b6 with check after promotion. Kc7 supports the resulting perpetual.

exercises.prompt: Why does the extra queen not win here?
exercises.answer: Black must answer a check on every turn, and its queen cannot interpose against a knight check or capture the protected knight.

startContext: The complete six-piece board is reconstructed from saved images. The source’s Nc6 check, Ne5/Nc4 reroute and Nxb6/Nc8 perpetual are checked exactly. Extra repetitions of the same forced checking cycle are independently extended to make threefold repetition explicit. The Nd4 comparison is independent.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
